## Overview

This spec holds the vectors that reproduce cases of Go's `crypto/x509` `verifyTests` for the `x509-verify` spec's `verify` function. The function, its types, its algorithm and its contracts are exactly those of `x509-verify`; nothing here changes them. The cases are kept in their own file because the real-world chains they carry are large.

Every vector uses the default purpose, `serverAuth`.

## Types

`VerifyError` is the `x509-verify` spec's.

## Functions

### verify

```pseudocode
verify(leaf_der: Bytes, intermediates_der: [Bytes], roots_der: [Bytes], host: String?, now_unix: Int, purpose: String = "serverAuth") -> [Bytes] | VerifyError
```

As defined by the `x509-verify` spec.

## Behavioral Contracts

**MUST:**

1. An implementation of `x509-verify` MUST pass these vectors as well as that spec's own.

## Test Vectors

The arguments are those of `x509-verify`: `leaf_der_hex`, `intermediates_der_hex`, `roots_der_hex`, `host` and `now_unix`. A success is an assertion on the returned chain: its length and the SHA-256 of each element, leaf first.

### Sources

- `go` vectors (7) reproduce cases of `verifyTests` in Go's `src/crypto/x509/verify_test.go` (master, fetched 2026-10-22): the certificates are that file's PEM constants, `now_unix` the case's `currentTime` and `host` its `dnsName`. The case name is a tag (`go-valid` is `Valid`). They are Valid, LeafInRoots, ExcludedNames, CriticalExtLeaf, ValidCN, AKIDNoSKID and the unnamed two-parent case after
  it. The expectations are this spec's and match Go's outcome except CriticalExtLeaf, `InvalidCertificate` (Go: an unhandled-critical-extension error).
- Go cases not reproduced: MissingIntermediate, Valid (fqdn), MixedCase, HostnameMismatch, IPMissing, Expired, RootInIntermediates, InvalidHash and LeafInRootsInvalid, which repeat 3 KB to 4 KB chains whose behaviour generated vectors cover (Expired, at time 1, is `NotYetValid` here; InvalidHash, signed with SHA-224, is `UnsupportedAlgorithm`); TooManyDNS and TooManyIPs, which test Go's error
  text; EKULeaf, EKULeafExplicit and MultipleConstraints, whose lines would exceed 10,000 characters; EKULeafValid, about email protection; X509v1Intermediate and CriticalExtIntermediate, whose leaves have no subjectAltName, so every host is `HostnameMismatch` first; IgnoreCNWithSANs, whose leaf has `*` in a PrintableString and is `InvalidCertificate`; and SHA-384, whose root is self-signed with
  SHA-1, so it is discarded and the result is `UnknownAuthority`.

## Edge Cases

- **Leaf in roots** (`go-leaf-in-roots`): the chain is the leaf alone.
- **An unhandled critical extension on the leaf** (`go-critical-ext-leaf`): `InvalidCertificate`.

## Implementation Notes

- These chains use RSA-2048 and P-256 keys from real and test hierarchies; they need no feature beyond `x509-verify`.

## References

- [Go crypto/x509](https://github.com/golang/go/tree/master/src/crypto/x509) -- `verify_test.go`, the source of these cases.
- [RFC 5280](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html) -- path validation (6.1).
